sections.html:
The Lorain County Recorder files deeds. The office is in Room 102 at 226 Middle Avenue, Elyria, OH 44035. Call 440-329-5148. Weekday hours are 8 AM to 4 PM, posted on the recorder's website.

The Recorder keeps the land record and nothing else. Staff do not supply blank forms, fill them in, alter a deed, decide ownership disputes, or search for liens for you. A title company or attorney covers those jobs. County records go back to 1824. You can download a free copy of your own deed from the online property search, and certified copies are available at the counter.

Two pages of a deed cost $39.00, and the price climbs by $8.00 with every added page. Each printed side is a page, so a deed printed on both faces of two sheets counts as four.

Lorain County Recorder charges for common filings
FilingCharge
Deed, mortgage, lease or affidavit, pages one and two$39.00
Page three and beyond, per page$8.00
Release, amendment or assignment (marginal notation)Recording fee plus $4.00 per notation
Plain copy$2.00 per page
Certified copy$2.00 per page, plus $1.00 for the seal
Real estate financing statement$12.00, plus $4.00 for each name indexed
Federal tax lien and its release$5.00 and $3.00
Living will or health care power of attorney$34.00 minimum, $40.00 maximum

The amount splits evenly between a basic fee and a contribution to the Ohio Housing Trust Fund. A $5.00 preservation surcharge from Senate Bill 94 is part of the present level. The fee chart shows three pages at $47.00, five at $63.00 and ten at $103.00.

sections.h2: The auditor endorses the deed first
sections.html:
Under section 319.202 of the Revised Code, the buyer files a value statement, then the Auditor marks the fee on the deed. The seller pays it.

The Auditor's transfer page sets rules that trip up late arrivals:

  • Transfers happen Monday through Thursday, 8 AM to 4 PM, so Friday closings need planning.
  • E-filed packets are cut off at 3 PM, and walk-ins at 4 PM.
  • The office refuses anything sent through the U.S. Postal Service.
  • Handwritten forms go back to the sender. Typed, fully completed forms only.
  • A packet with a missing form or the wrong payment is returned, never held.

Staff may not fill out the conveyance or exempt form or give advice about it, citing section 4705.01. Your closing agent or attorney should assemble the packet and confirm the amounts with the Auditor's office in advance.

sections.h2: How the conveyance fee is set
sections.html:
Ohio law fixes the base at a one dollar minimum, or ten cents for each $100 or fraction of $100 of value, whichever is more, in section 319.54(G)(3). A county commission may add a transfer tax of as much as thirty cents per $100 under section 322.02. Phone the Auditor for the combined Lorain County rate before you estimate your net proceeds.

Many transfers owe no conveyance fee, though the form must say why. Common cases for families include gifts between spouses or from parents to children, deeds among heirs of one estate where no money is paid, and moves into or out of a revocable trust. Every transfer, exempt or not, also pays fifty cents for each parcel.

Documents prepared after June 30, 2009 must meet the standardization rules of section 317.114, and the Recorder adds $20.00 when they miss. The fee page spells out font size, ink color, paper size, a three inch blank band on page one and margins on every side, and offers a downloadable template. Court papers, plats, DD-214 discharges and state or federal documents are exempt.

Have the preparer check the template before signing, since a rejected deed costs a second trip to Elyria. The Recorder does not help complete forms, so the preparer is your only safeguard here.

Lorain County stretches along Lake Erie west of Cuyahoga County. Elyria holds the courthouse, while the city of Lorain has the most residents. The county had an estimated 323,219 residents in July 2025 and 139,777 housing units. A typical owned home is worth $223,200, and owners live in 74.0 percent of homes. Median gross rent is $966. Most Lorain County sales therefore involve an owner-occupied house with a deed and mortgage already on file.

Sign up for the free property alert service on the Recorder's website. Deed fraud means criminals transferring a property without the owner's knowledge. Check your records and be wary of unsolicited deed offers.

Before you list a house, search your own parcel online and confirm the last recorded deed carries the name of the person who will sign. If an old mortgage was paid off but its release never reached the record, have it recorded, at the $4.00 marginal notation charge.

An owner who served can record a DD-214 or NGB-22 so a safe copy exists if the original is lost. The records are protected, and only the person named or an authorized person can see them. One certified copy of a service discharge is free.
Since each extra page adds $8.00, ask your preparer to keep the deed brief. A reference to an older recorded document also triggers the $4.00 notation charge.

sections.h2: What goes in the closing packet
sections.html:
Assemble these items so neither office sends you back:

  • The signed, notarized deed, typed, with the legal description and every parcel number.
  • The right conveyance form, or the exempt form with its reason written out.
  • Payment to the Auditor for the conveyance fee and the per-parcel charge.
  • A check to the Recorder sized to the page count.
  • A check that each page is in black or blue ink and has the margins the template calls for.

Because the Auditor cuts off e-files at 3 PM on transfer days, line up the vendor early on the day you close. The order is simple: the Auditor first, then the Recorder, one floor of the same building apart.

faqs.q: What does Lorain County charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: The fee page prints $39.00 for the first two pages and $8.00 per page after that. A $4.00 notation applies to each release or assignment, and a layout violation adds $20.00. The Auditor's conveyance fee is paid separately.

faqs.q: Will the Lorain County Auditor take a deed by mail?
faqs.a: No. Mailed transfers are refused. Deliver the packet in person Monday through Thursday or send it through an approved e-file vendor before 3 PM.

faqs.q: Can the Lorain County Recorder fix a mistake on my deed?
faqs.a: No. The Recorder cannot alter a deed and is not trained to search for liens for you. An attorney can prepare a corrective deed, which the Recorder then files.

faqs.q: Who bills property tax in Lorain County?
faqs.a: The County Treasurer and County Auditor handle tax bills. The Recorder only keeps the documents that show who owns the land.

faqs.q: Where can I see an old Lorain County deed?
faqs.a: Use the online property search on the Recorder's website to view and download a free copy. Records reach back to 1824, and certified copies are available in person.
